column1: # #1023 A/B shared oracle for what a wrapper or a host returns before a collection starts, measured with Java
# (NamedCapture / SemanticPredicateParser / CaptureBoundaryParser.input), columns as full.tsv. Every column runs under a
# root SemanticPredicateScope(["t"]) whose predicate t always holds (SP needs it); the shapes of empty-token.tsv measure the
# same values with or without it. SemanticPredicateParser (SP, predicate t), SemanticPredicateScope (SPS),
# NameResolutionScope (NRS) and CaptureScope (CS) are not CollectingParsers: like NamedCapture (Own), Commit (Cmt), Label
# (Lbl) and InvertMatchPropagationStopper (SI) they return what their child returned, so SP[Opt[z]] returns Optional's
# empty token. DoConsumePropagationStopper (SC; Rust stop_consume) is Classic. Hosts (Rust Custom) return what they
# returned, which a later collection collects in order: h0 returns Token(consumed, peek(cursor, 0)), an empty consumed
# token, so the collection starts at its position as after a collector; hn returns no token (Parsed.SUCCEEDED), so a later
# child of another kind leaves "" at the consumed cursor as after !z; hv returns an empty token of the virtualTokenConsumed
# kind, excluded by its kind as vc is; hc returns a consumed token of the input 'c' without consuming it, which is
# collected; h1 returns a consumed token of 'c' and consumes it; hx returns an empty consumed token of the input at 0, away
# from the cursor, where the collection then starts unless an earlier child returned a token first
# (Chain[Opt[z],hx,vc] starts at the cursor). Not here, where Rust differs from Java as before #1023 A/B: hx and hc alone
# and Chain[hc,c] (no collection starts), hx before an empty collector (Chain[hx,Opt[z],vc], Chain[hx,E,vci],
# Ord[hx,Opt[z],vci]) and the value boundaries over a host projection after a host (Chain[h0,proj], Chain[hn,proj],
# Chain[hn,proj0]). Other shapes as full.tsv / empty-token.tsv, whose shapes are not repeated here.
